title_en: Guiding Opinions on Establishing and Improving the Working Mechanism for Protecting the Legitimate Rights and Interests of the Elderly
full_text_en:
Ministry of Civil Affairs, National Office on Aging, Supreme People's Court
Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of Justice, China National Committee on Aging

Guiding Opinions on Establishing and Improving the Working Mechanism for Protecting the Lawful Rights and Interests of the Elderly

Minfa [2025] No. 26

Departments (Bureaus) of Civil Affairs, Offices of the Committee on Aging, High People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, Departments (Bureaus) of Public Security, Departments (Bureaus) of Justice of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Bureau of Civil Affairs, Office of the Committee on Aging of Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps; the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region High People's Court Production and Construction Corps Branch; the People's Procuratorate, Public Security Bureau, and Justice Bureau of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

Establishing and improving a working mechanism for protecting the lawful rights and interests of the elderly is an urgent requirement for safeguarding the dignity and rights of the elderly and building an age-friendly society. It is conducive to enhancing the well-being of the elderly and promoting family harmony and social harmony. In order to implement the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of the Rights and Interests of the Elderly, implement the national strategy of actively responding to population aging, further improve the work of protecting the rights and interests of the elderly, accelerate the construction of a collaborative and interconnected working mechanism at all levels and across departments, and enable the vast number of elderly people to share the fruits of reform and development and enjoy a happy old age, the following opinions are hereby put forward.

I. General Requirements

Adhere to the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, thoroughly implement the guiding principles of the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China and the Second and Third Plenary Sessions of the 20th Central Committee, strengthen the Party's overall leadership over aging-related work, adhere to a people-centered approach, focus on new situations, new problems, and new trends in the protection of the rights and interests of the elderly, integrate the concept of protecting the rights and interests of the elderly into the entire process of social governance, improve the working mechanism, strengthen coordination and linkage, form a closed loop of risk early warning and prevention, dispute discovery and reporting, and dispute resolution and handling, better protect the lawful rights and interests of the elderly in accordance with the law, and continuously enhance the elderly's sense of gain, happiness, and security.

II. Strengthening Risk Early Warning and Prevention Related to the Elderly

(1) Focus on risk source prevention. Closely monitor various types of disputes and major incidents related to the elderly, regularly conduct situation analysis and judgment, and strengthen risk monitoring and early warning. Focus on risk prevention in areas such as elderly care consumption, support and inheritance, financial management, and health and wellness, and do a good job in legal education lectures, professional consultation, and special guidance to enhance the elderly's ability to resist risks. Promote relevant functional departments to strengthen risk supervision and special governance, reducing the occurrence of disputes related to the elderly at the source.

(2) Carry out rights protection publicity and education. Implement the responsibility system for legal education that "those who enforce the law shall also popularize the law", include the publicity and education of the Law on the Protection of the Rights and Interests of the Elderly in the legal education responsibility list, comprehensively enhance the legal literacy of the elderly group and the whole society, and raise the legal awareness of respecting, loving, assisting, and protecting the elderly throughout society. Use important time points such as "Elderly Respect Month" to widely carry out publicity and education activities on the rights protection of the elderly. Establish and improve the mechanism for publishing typical cases of protection of the rights and interests of the elderly, enhance the awareness of the elderly in using legal means to protect their own lawful rights and interests, and improve the elderly's ability to identify and prevent fraud.

(3) Create a social support environment. Promote communities with a high degree of population aging, as well as elderly care service institutions, social organizations related to the elderly, and other institutions and venues where the elderly concentrate, to carry out diverse forms of publicity and education activities on the protection of the rights and interests of the elderly through public lectures, legal consultations, case-based explanations, public service advertisements, etc., creating a favorable social atmosphere for protecting the lawful rights and interests of the elderly throughout society.

III. Strengthening the Discovery and Reporting of Disputes Related to the Elderly

(4) Give full play to the role of service hotlines. Strengthen the docking and linkage of the 12368 litigation service hotline, the 12309 procuratorial service hotline, and the 12348 public legal service hotline; accept in a timely manner in accordance with the law legal consultations or complaints and reports involving the elderly's marriage and family, property rights confirmation, personal injury, etc.; and strengthen the full-process management of acceptance, verification, handling, and feedback of the elderly's demands.

(5) Unblock channels for discovery and reporting. Village (resident) committees, social work service institutions, community neighbors, public welfare organizations, volunteers, and practitioners in related industries who discover that the lawful rights and interests of the elderly are being infringed upon have the right to promptly dissuade and assist the elderly to report to relevant units and seek help, provide necessary psychological counseling and psychological support to the relevant elderly, and help the elderly who suffer from domestic violence, abandonment, abuse, or other physical or mental infringement to report to public security organs or file lawsuits with people's courts. Where conditions are met, public security organs, village (resident) committees, rescue management agencies, etc., may apply to the people's court on behalf of the elderly for a personal safety protection order.

IV. Properly Resolving and Handling Disputes Related to the Elderly

(6) Promote dispute resolution. Give full play to the positive role of townships (subdistricts), village (resident) committees, social organizations, people's mediation committees, etc., in mediating family disputes such as elderly marriage, guardianship, and support, and help the elderly and their families solve problems and resolve disputes in a timely manner. Local civil affairs departments and offices of the committee on aging shall coordinate with people's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, judicial administrative departments, etc., to carry out the resolution of major disputes related to the elderly and strengthen source prevention and control.

(7) Strengthen judicial protection for disputes related to the elderly. People's courts shall accept cases for filing, hear, and enforce cases involving infringement of the lawful rights and interests of the elderly in a timely manner in accordance with the law. They shall provide guarantees for facilitating the elderly's participation in litigation activities, improve barrier-free facilities and services in litigation service venues; provide online litigation services for the elderly with limited mobility, or provide multiple services such as appointment filing and door-to-door filing, while retaining traditional litigation service methods that are easily accepted by the elderly. Depending on the circumstances of the case, relevant auxiliary or accompanying personnel may be allowed to accompany the elderly party to appear in court. People's procuratorates shall, relying on areas such as barrier-free environment construction, food and drug safety, and anti-telecommunications network fraud, carry out procuratorial public interest litigation for the protection of the rights and interests of the elderly, and safeguard the lawful rights and interests of many elderly people. Give full play to the procuratorial organs' function of supporting civil prosecution, and legally support the prosecution of cases where the elderly with weak litigation ability seek alimony or support payments.

(8) Increase the intensity of handling disputes related to the elderly. People's courts, people's procuratorates, and public security organs shall intensify the crackdown on illegal and criminal activities related to the elderly, and legally punish theft, robbery, snatching, extortion of property from the elderly, and illegal and criminal acts such as infringing upon the property rights and interests of the elderly through fraudulent means under the guise of "elderly care". Where abuse or abandonment of the elderly constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law. Legally and severely crack down on criminal acts such as intentional injury that seriously infringe upon the personal rights of the elderly. Procuratorial organs at all levels shall give full play to their role in legal supervision, legally increase the crackdown and punishment on various illegal and criminal acts that infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of the elderly, and through procuratorial functions such as public interest litigation, urge relevant departments to fulfill their comprehensive supervision duties in accordance with the law, and strengthen source governance.

V. Improving the Quality of Services for Protecting the Rights of the Elderly

(9) Enhance the intensity of legal services. Judicial administrative departments shall strengthen the construction of public legal service workstations in townships (subdistricts) and public legal service offices in villages (communities), and provide convenient and efficient legal services such as legal consultation and drafting of legal documents for the elderly. They shall provide barrier-free legal services for the elderly, and provide barrier-free facilities and equipment according to actual conditions. For the elderly who have suffered abuse, abandonment, or domestic violence, applying for legal aid shall not be subject to economic hardship conditions; for the elderly with no fixed source of income, and for the elderly receiving social assistance or judicial assistance, the verification of economic hardship status shall be exempted when applying for legal aid. Increase the intensity of legal aid, and legally include eligible elderly persons such as those who are very old, empty-nest, living alone, disabled or cognitively impaired, and from special family planning families into the scope of legal aid. Encourage social forces to actively participate in volunteer legal aid services for the elderly, and establish a normalized and professional legal service team for the elderly.

(10) Give full play to the role of professional talents. Judicial administrative departments shall guide lawyers and the notary industry to take the elderly as key targets of public legal services, encourage and support lawyers and lawyer industry associations to participate in legal service activities for the elderly, and carry out business training and exchange seminars related to the protection of the rights and interests of the elderly, so as to improve the level of legal services for the elderly. They shall, focusing on the needs of the elderly, give full play to the role of diverse composite talent teams including social workers and legal workers, integrate multiple resources to provide convenient, efficient, scientific, and professional services for the elderly, and meet the growing needs of the elderly for rights protection.

VI. Strengthening Organization and Implementation

Under the leadership of Party committees and governments at all levels, establish and improve a coordination mechanism for the protection of the rights and interests of the elderly, promote communication, information sharing, and exchange and consultation among civil affairs departments, people's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, judicial administrative departments, etc., and study and solve prominent problems in the protection of the rights and interests of the elderly in a timely manner. Local civil affairs departments and offices of the committee on aging shall strengthen overall coordination, do a good job in evaluation and statistical surveys of the work of protecting the rights and interests of the elderly, and, in accordance with relevant legal provisions, commend or reward advanced models in protecting the lawful rights and interests of the elderly. People's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, and judicial administrative departments shall, in light of their own work responsibilities and professional advantages, increase their work intensity and jointly perform the work of protecting the rights and interests of the elderly well. All localities shall explore promoting the establishment of an overall coordination mechanism for aging work in townships (subdistricts) and a mechanism for designated persons to take responsibility, firmly compact and consolidate the responsibility for protecting the rights and interests of the elderly, and truly safeguard the rights and interests of the elderly.

April 30, 2025
